subject: Cross-border pricing & data residency options
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@acmerobotics.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing question: EU vs US rates + data residency adder

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement wants to confirm a few things before we move to an MSA review:

- Can you send a clean rate card (hosted API) showing baseline per-token rates for US and EU regions? We need clear line items for text gen and embeddings.
- Is there a separate data residency/hosting adder for the EU region (we need to keep EU customer data in-region)? If so, what is the adder (absolute or percentage) and how is it invoiced (EUR or USD)?
- What discount scales do you offer for annual committed spend? Any examples for a 12–18 month commit at ~$250k ARR?

Could you attach the current rate card and a short note summarizing the residency adders so we can circulate to finance?

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Robotics

[Attachment: initial-acme-usage.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhang <alice@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 11:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pricing question: EU vs US rates + data residency adder

Hi Alice,

Appreciate the clear list — attaching the most up-to-date rate card and a short EU surcharge table for reference. High level:

- Baseline hosted API public rates (USD): text generation $0.0006 / token, embeddings $0.0004 / 1K tokens. See Redwood-RateCard-v3.pdf for full breakdown (we publish per-model variants as well).
- EU data residency adder: we offer a region-residency fee that covers in-region storage, private control plane connectivity, and additional logging retention. For hosted customers, the adder is currently a flat +12% on applicable usage that is pinned to EU-only hosting.
  - Invoicing: we can invoice in USD or EUR; by default we invoice USD and will apply a currency conversion with a small FX fee. If you prefer EUR invoicing, we can switch for contract purposes.
- Discounting: for a 12–18 month committed spend at the ~$250k ARR level, standard commercial guidance is 18–22% off baseline published rates (higher for multi-year or Dedicated commitments). We typically structure this as a committed spend credit applied monthly against usage.

If you want tighter economics I can put together two options: (A) hosted with 12% EU adder + 20% commit discount, or (B) Dedicated reserved pool (no per-region adder, lower unit cost) — option B requires a minimum monthly commit and a short procurement lead time.

Next steps: can you share expected monthly usage profile (tokens/month), preferred invoice currency, and whether EU residency must be enforced for all traffic or only customer-submitted PII? I can have Sales Ops produce a redline-able proposal by EOD Thursday.

Attachments: Redwood-RateCard-v3.pdf, eu-surcharge-table.csv

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Sergio — forwarding guidance from Sales Ops as discussed. TL;DR: allow up to 22% discount for this ARR band if customer signs 12 month commit and accepts USD invoicing. Recommended commercial structure:

- Option 1 (Hosted + Residency): baseline rates less 20% commit discount, plus 12% EU residency adder applied to EU-scoped usage. Invoice USD monthly.
- Option 2 (Dedicated): converted to a reserved capacity SKU with ~28% effective discount vs public rates (no residency adder). Requires 3-month ramp and longer lead time.

Attached is a draft proposal (acme-proposal-draft.docx) with placeholders for token volumes. We should get procurement's invoice currency preference before finalizing.

If you want sign-off above 22% we need an approval ticket (finance); otherwise you have spending authority to offer up to 22%.

-Monica

Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sergio and Monica — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we circulate to finance/procurement: 

- Can you confirm the residency adder applies only to hosted API usage that you explicitly pin to EU region? (i.e., we can choose to run some workloads in US and not pay the adder)
- If we take Option 1 with USD invoicing, can procurement request EUR invoices during contracting and have the contract lock EUR pricing? Procurement prefers EUR for their ledgers.
- Last: do you have a sample SLA clause or residency appendix we can include in the MSA? We need explicit commitments on where logs and backups are kept and a 30 day notice for data export.

If those answers look good we are ready to move to an MSA review — can you send a DocuSign for the commercial sheet so we can get internal signatures?

Best,
Alice
